g.text: The continuous RC floor and its real boundary cuts
Development comparison. Installed material, air, moisture and site evidence remain open.
A SERVICE-SPINE SECTION / cropped field
Continuous RC200 upper lift, Z−380..−180.
Possible prepared lower-grid interface at Z−380.
DPC band Z−180..−30. Plaster begins at Z0.
The wall core bridges the 30 mm between DPC and plaster.
Connected lower concrete can carry ground moisture.
Geometry and scope shown separately from performance.
B ONE POUR / ACTUAL QUANTITIES
104.895 m² physical slab and seat.
20.979 m³ gross RC at nominal depth.
3.725 t steel before laps and edges.
6.561 t cement in the trial batch.
Zero-air sensitivity exceeds the 25 kN/m³ load bound.
C D1800 STRESS COMPARISON
Slab soffit, 1070 mm vertical clearance.
Lowest girder, 700 mm vertical clearance.
Lowest cap, 700 mm vertical clearance.
Separate full water track, 262 mm vertical clearance.
Actual free openings, drainage and soil exposure remain open.
D ONE FLOOR/WALL AIR FAMILY
63.235 m³/h at 50 Pa, provisional.
Slab, actual cracks, 22 wall bases and ordinary perimeter.
Three RC crossings and the unresolved lower stair toe.
Complete doors and service penetrations have separate cuts.
Actual contributions remain unmeasured.
Glass stays above the structural pour.
The comparison retains the accessible service zone.
